title: Autograph letter signed, Weymouth, 16 July 1799
text: Dr. Cotton Tufts writes from Weymouth to Rev. Stephen Peabody, settling money held in trust for Mrs. Peabody: he has left forty-five dollars and sixty cents “with the President’s Lady” (Abigail Adams) for the sums due and for the last quarter’s rent on the Medford farm. Elizabeth (Smith) Shaw Peabody was Abigail’s sister and Rev. Peabody’s wife. The catalogue gives Tufts’s birth year as 1734; this site follows 1732. Sold at iCollector, 25 October 2007, for $140 plus buyer’s premium.
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: iCollector lot page

title: Autograph letter signed to Dr. Philip Draper, Weymouth, 26 October 1785
text: The sheet behind the 1785 Draper letter described under Letters and Papers at Auction. Tufts declines an invitation to an association of physicians and asks how the society has proceeded. It was offered by University Archives on 6 December 2016 (estimate $800–$1,000) and is marked as having passed.
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: University Archives lot page

title: Abington selectmen and committee of correspondence to Cotton Tufts at Weymouth, 1 June 1775
text: A folded letter carried privately and addressed to Tufts as chairman of the committees of Cohasset, Hingham, Weymouth and Braintree. It begins “Pursuant to your letter (of the 30 of May)…” and is attested by Daniel Noyes, clerk, for the Abington selectmen and committee of correspondence, two weeks before Bunker Hill. It is addressed to him, not written by him. Offered by Schuyler Rumsey Philatelic Auctions, Sale 55, lot 349 (estimate $3,000–$4,000; opening bid $2,900). No lot photograph is shown.
label: Rumsey lot page
flag: The realized price of the Abington letter, and whether it sold, has not been found on a public page. Note: Pending further work.

title: Deed signed by John and Abigail Adams, 9 April 1803
text: A printed form completed in John Adams’s hand and signed by John and Abigail Adams, recording the sale of land at Braintree to Cotton Tufts Jr. Bonhams explains that Norton Quincy (1716–1801), Abigail’s uncle, left no children, so his lands passed to her, and calls the purchaser a cousin of Abigail. The document is in the Adamses’ names; Tufts is the grantee. Sold at Bonhams, New York, 21 November 2023 (sale 28447, lot 57), for $8,320 including premium.
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: Bonhams lot page

title: Town of Weymouth receipt, 19 February 1833
text: The Town of Weymouth bought 15⅞ pounds of butter “of Tufts & Whitten” for $2.54, and payment was received for the firm by a hand the listing reads as J. Byron. Cotton Tufts Jr. died at Weymouth later in 1833, so he was living when the receipt was written; the hand is not his. The sheet is offered on eBay (asking $59.77 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 206598016754
flag: The firm is written “Tufts & Whitten,” not Tufts & Whittemore, the name on this page; that they are the same Weymouth store is an inference from the name and the town, and the receipt does not name Cotton Tufts Jr. Note: Pending further work.

title: Notice to the Newburyport selectmen, 11 July 1766, offered as a 1766 “indenture”
text: The photograph, from a Josephmarc listing of eBay item 860119781812, is of the notice dated 11 July 1766 in which “Saml Tufts” tells the selectmen of Newburyport that on 7 July he had taken into his family Samuel Resnick, about eight, son of Isaac Resnick, late of Newbury. That is the same text already shown on Samuel Tufts (several men). The dealer titled the lot a colonial indenture and reported a date of 7 February 1766; the sheet itself is dated 11 July. Asking $395 when last seen (28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: Josephmarc listing
flag: Unverified. The photograph shows the July 1766 selectmen notice already on this site, not a February indenture; the dealer’s February date is a misreading of the sheet. Whether this listing is a later sale of the same piece already photographed from another eBay offer has not been confirmed from the paper itself. Whether the writer is Dr. Samuel Tufts (1735–1799), rather than another Samuel Tufts, still rests only on the name and place. Note: Pending further work.

title: Charlestown tax assessors’ account books, 1780–1782
text: Ten small octavo account books of Charlestown real-estate and poll taxes, signed by “various Charlestown tax assessors, including Sam Swan, Timothy Tufts, and others,” were sold at Skinner, Boston, on 11 November 2019 (sale 3311T, lot 1023) for $923.75, against an estimate of $300–$400. Edward C. Booth records that Timothy Tufts (1735–1805) was a selectman of Charlestown for most of the years between 1780 and 1792 (“The Tufts Family in Somerville,” Historic Leaves, vol. 1, p. 25). No lot photograph is shown.
label: Skinner lot page
flag: Unverified. The lot names only “Timothy Tufts.” Charlestown had other men of that name in 1780–1782, among them this man’s son Timothy (b. 1762), and the books have not been seen. Attaching the signature to Timothy Tufts (1735–1805) rests on his public office. Note: Pending further work.

title: T. Tufts & Co. letterhead, Alstead, N.H., 1873
text: A letter on the printed heading of T. Tufts & Co., Dry and Fancy Goods, Hats, Caps, Clothing, Boots and Shoes, dated at Alstead in 1873. The listing places it at “Alstead NY,” but the heading reads N.H. It is offered on eBay (asking $19.50 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 335676096203
flag: The heading gives only “T. Tufts & Co.” Attaching it to Timothy Tufts rests on the trade, the town, and Hurd’s statement that he conducted the Alstead business alone from 1851; the writer of the letter has not been identified. Note: Pending further work.

title: Auditor’s certificate, Virginia City, 18 May 1868
text: An auditor’s certificate of Montana Territory, dated at Virginia City on 18 May 1868, certifies that “James Tufts” had deposited territorial warrants with the Auditor, who was authorized to issue bonds for the sum. Tufts was then Secretary of the Territory. The certificate sold on eBay on 6 September 2026 for $29.99.
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 307166462503
flag: The certificate names only “James Tufts.” That he is the Territorial Secretary rests on the name, the town (then the territorial capital) and the year. Note: Pending further work.

title: Letter from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology to Prof. J. Tufts, Exeter, N.H., 21 September 1889
text: James P. Munroe, writing on Institute of Technology paper, tells the Exeter teacher that the faculty has voted to give a student, Mr. Bowers, credit for four subjects passed in the June examinations and to admit him if he passes the rest in June or September 1890. The letter is addressed to “Prof. J. Tufts, Exeter, N.H.” It is offered on eBay (asking $180.50 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 206629631012
flag: The letter names only “Prof. J. Tufts.” The identification with James Arthur Tufts rests on the town and on his post at Phillips Exeter Academy in 1889. Note: Pending further work.

title: Letter of William A. Bancroft, Cambridge, 3 November 1903
text: Written from Arborcroft, Ware Street, Cambridge, to “My Dear Tufts”: “We send you our deepest sympathy and hope that Mrs Tufts is not seriously injured.” It is one of three letters of condolence of November and December 1903 that are offered on eBay by one seller (asking $203.06 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 117468320868

title: Letter of Marshall Snow, Washington University, St. Louis, 9 November 1903
text: Addressed to “Dear Mr. Tufts” and written on Washington University paper, it begins: “I have just heard of the great sorrow that has come to your household.” Offered on eBay (asking $128.60 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 206731391595

title: Letter of Pitts Duffield, Fox, Duffield & Company, New York, December 1903
text: Written on the letterhead of the publishers Fox, Duffield & Company to “My dear Mr. Tufts.” As far as the photograph can be read, the writer has learned of the family’s loss through the News-Letter and mentions a daughter. The listing dates it 14 December; the dateline on the photograph appears to read the 8th. Offered on eBay (asking $248.19 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 117468320912
flag: The three 1903 letters: the eBay titles give them to “Dr. James H. Tufts,” “Philosopher James H Tufts” and “Prof. Albert Tufts,” and the letters themselves say only “Tufts.” They are placed here because the Bancroft letter of 3 November hopes that “Mrs Tufts” is not seriously injured, one day after the accident that killed Effie Miriam Tufts, and the Duffield letter appears to cite the News-Letter. The photographs do not name the addressee, and the 8th or 14th of December for the Duffield letter has not been settled. Note: Pending further work.

title: John Hancock, as Governor, to Cotton Tufts, Boston, 10 April 1788
text: The letter described under Letters and Papers at Auction, photographed at the 2021 RR Auction sale. Hancock summons “Honble Cotton Tufts Esqr” to a committee “to enquire into the State of the College” at 10 o’clock on the following Tuesday. The address leaf is shown below.

title: Autograph letter signed, Weymouth, 15 October 1772
text: The family letter described under Letters and Papers at Auction, later sold at Christie’s, New York, on 12 June 1996, for $115. The Christie’s lot page carries no photograph of the letter.
label: Christie’s lot page
flag: The catalogue called the recipient his daughter; the only child recorded of Dr. Cotton Tufts and Lucy Quincy is their son Cotton Jr., and the Shute address in the Weymouth papers points to him. The original address leaf has not been seen here. Note: Pending further work.

title: Abigail Adams dinner invitation, 31 December 1807
text: The dinner invitation of 31 December 1807, described under A New Year’s Dinner Invitation, 1807. The upper leaf is addressed to “Mr Cotton Tufts and Lady, Weymouth.” The note, dated at Quincy, reads: “The president and Mrs Adams ask the pleasure of mr and Mrs Tufts company to dinner tomorrow 2 oclock, together with mr Quincy Tufts and miss Lucy.” The photographs are from the 2025 RR Auction sale.
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: RR Auction lot page (2025)
flag: The 2025 RR Auction catalogue attributes the invitation to the physician Dr. Cotton Tufts rather than to Cotton Jr. and Mercy. The 2014 catalogue, and the family dates, identify the younger household. Note: Pending further work.

title: Abigail Adams dinner invitation, 31 December 1807
text: The invitation names “mr Quincy Tufts,” then sixteen, with his parents and his sister Lucy. The letter and its later sales are described on the page of his father, Cotton Tufts (1757–1833).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: RR Auction lot page (2025)

title: Abigail Adams dinner invitation, 31 December 1807
text: The invitation is addressed to “Mr Cotton Tufts and Lady, Weymouth.” That the lady is Mercy rests on the 2014 catalogue’s reading of the household, not on her name in the text. The letter is described on the page of her husband, Cotton Tufts (1757–1833).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: RR Auction lot page (2025)
flag: The identification of Mercy as the “Lady” invited with Cotton Jr. depends on the 2014 RR Auction catalogue, not on her name. Note: Pending further work.

text: The whole sheet of the survey already shown on this page: “This Plan Laid down by a Scale of Half-Mile per inch By Peter Tufts junior June 14th 1797,” ink and watercolor on two joined sheets. Offered by Boston Rare Maps (sold; price not shown).
who: Boston Rare Maps (dealer’s photograph, inventory BRM3348)
lic: Manuscript of 1797, public domain

title: Harvard Square Furniture and Job Wagon billhead, 2 November 1885
text: A bill of Samuel Tufts, office at the Lyceum Exchange, Harvard Square, residence 890 Main Street, to Mrs. C. E. Choate, for work in a house and for changing furniture, totaling $3.00. Payment is receipted “Saml Tufts per” another hand. The heading calls the firm the oldest of its kind in Old Cambridge, established in 1868. Offered on eBay (asking $16.45 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 287420652806

title: Worcester County writ, directed to a Dudley constable, signed Aaron Tufts
text: A printed Commonwealth of Massachusetts form, filled in by hand, commands the sheriff of Worcester County or a constable of the Town of Dudley to levy a judgment recovered before “Aaron Tufts Esquire, one of the Justices of the Peace.” It is signed Aaron Tufts. The listing dates the writ to 1825 and ties it to a sheriff’s sale of the Bemis & Shepard textile mills. Offered on eBay (asking $149.95 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 206581928259
flag: The year 1825, and the connection with a Bemis & Shepard mill sale, come from the listing and a printed card in the photograph, not from a complete reading of the faded handwriting. Note: Pending further work.

title: Docket of an 1811 cotton-trade letter or invoice
text: The photograph is of a wrapper or docket only, reading “Gardner Tufts / Cotton 1811.” The letter or invoice itself is not shown. Offered on eBay (asking $1,000.00 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 128127237207
flag: Unverified identity. The docket names only “Gardner Tufts” and the year 1811. This is not Gardiner Tufts of Lynn, who was not born until 1828. A merchant Gardner Tufts of Brookfield, later of Savannah, born 15 July 1777, was then living and in trade, and died at sea in 1824; that he is the man named on this wrapper has not been shown. Note: Pending further work.

title: Jamaica Plain Gas Light Company bill, 1 July 1901
text: A printed bill of the Jamaica Plain Gas Light Company, dated 1 July 1901. The eBay title gives it as a bill of George Tufts. Offered on eBay (asking $9.09 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 306759542211
flag: Unverified. The name George Tufts is not readable on the photograph held here; it is taken from the listing title only. It has not been shown that the account belonged to George F. Tufts (1825–1920) of Charlestown and Medford, or to any other man already on this site. Note: Pending further work.

title: Tufts & Neal billhead, Main Street, Rangeley, Maine
text: A blank bill form headed “To TUFTS & NEAL, Dr., Main St.,” with a printed date line of the 1890s and the place Rangeley, Me. The partner’s first name is not given. Offered on eBay (asking $7.99 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 350345003166
flag: Unverified identity. The heading gives only the firm name. A Baker Tufts, boat builder, born 26 May 1823 at Farmington, Maine, died at Rangeley on 27 July 1898, is recorded in the family record (Tufts Kinsmen, Vol. I, p. 282, no. 155-6); it has not been shown that he was the Tufts of this firm. Note: Pending further work.

title: Billhead of Drs. Packer & Tufts, Virginia City, Nevada
text: A printed bill form of “Drs. Packer & Tufts,” Virginia City, Nev., with a date line of the 1880s, made out for medicine. The first name of Dr. Tufts is not on the sheet. The lot sold on eBay on 14 October 2026 for $24.95.
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 800795075998
flag: The billhead does not give Dr. Tufts’s first name. William Harvey King, History of Homœopathy and Its Institutions in America (New York, 1905), the Nevada chapter by Thomas Lindsley Bradford, lists “Tufts, J. E., Virginia City,” among homœopathic physicians in Nevada before 1886, and “Packer, Fred H., Virginia City,” as beginning practice in 1871. That J. E. Tufts is the partner on this bill has not been shown from the sheet itself. Note: Pending further work.

title: Letterhead of John M. Tufts, Tufts Roll-Top Desks, 12 February 1892
text: A letter on the printed heading of John M. Tufts, manufacturer of fine bank and office furniture and of “the celebrated Tufts Roll-Top Desks,” 131 Fulton Street, northeast corner of Nassau, New York, with the factory at Somerville, Massachusetts. It is dated 12 February 1892 and signed John M. Tufts, and discusses a shipment of desks from the Boston factory. The lot sold on eBay on 4 September 2026 for $12.50.
